Since the maps $p$ and $q$ are smooth of relative dimension $\dim(K)$, we have canonical isomorphisms $p^{!}\cong p^{*}[\dim(K)]$ and $q^{!}\cong q^{*}[\dim(K)]$, so that the condition (A.5) can be replaced by $q^{!}(\mathscr{F}_{1}\,\widetilde{\boxtimes}\,\mathscr{F}_{2})\cong p^{!}(\mathscr{F}_{1}\mathchoice{\mathbin{\mathop{\boxtimes}^{L}}_{\mathbf{k}}}{\boxtimes^{L}_{\mathbf{k}}}{\boxtimes^{L}_{\mathbf{k}}}{\boxtimes^{L}_{\mathbf{k}}}\mathscr{F}_{2})$.

In the special case considered for the geometric Satake equivalence, when $\mathbf{k}$ is not a field one modifies this construction slightly so that it sends pairs of perverse sheaves to perverse sheaves; see §10.3.

A.4 The case of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$

The main object of study in these notes is the category $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$. This setting does not fit exactly in the framework of §§A.1–A.3 because ${G_{\mathcal{K}}}$ and ${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ are not algebraic groups in the usual sense. But the category $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ still makes sense, as follows.

For any $n\in\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 1}$, we denote by $H_{n}\subset{G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ the kernel of the morphism

$G_{\mathcal{O}}\to G_{\mathcal{O}/t^{n}\mathcal{O}}$

induced by the quotient morphism $\mathcal{O}\to\mathcal{O}/t^{n}\mathcal{O}$. (Here the group scheme $G_{\mathcal{O}/t^{n}\mathcal{O}}$ is defined in a way similar to $G_{\mathcal{O}}$.) Note that if $m\geq n$, then $H_{m}$ is a normal subgroup in $H_{n}$, and the quotient $H_{n}/H_{m}$ is a unipotent group. If $X\subset\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ is a closed finite union of ${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -orbits, there exists $n\in\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 1}$ such that $H_{n}$ acts trivially on $X$. Then it makes sense to consider the equivariant derived category $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}/H_{n}}(X,\mathbf{k})$. Since $H_{n}/H_{m}$ is unipotent for any $m\geq n$, one can check using [BL, Theorem 3.7.3] that the functor

$D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}/H_{n}}(X,\mathbf{k})\to D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}/H_{m}}(X,\mathbf{k})$

given by inverse image under the projection $G/H_{m}\to G/H_{n}$ is an equivalence of categories. Hence one can define the category $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(X,\mathbf{k})$ to be $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}/H_{n}}(X,\mathbf{k})$ for any $n$ such that $H_{n}$ acts trivially on $X$.

If $X\subset Y\subset\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ are closed finite unions of ${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -orbits, the direct image under the embedding $X\hookrightarrow Y$ induces a fully-faithful functor $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(X,\mathbf{k})\to D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Y,\mathbf{k})$. Hence we can finally define $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ as the union of the categories $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(X,\mathbf{k})$ for all closed finite unions of ${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -orbits $X\subset\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$.

A construction similar to that of §A.3 produces a convolution bifunctor $\star$ on the category $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$. More precisely, if $\mathscr{F}_{1}$ and $\mathscr{F}_{2}$ are in $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$, one should choose a closed finite union of ${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -orbits $X\subset\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ such that $\mathscr{F}_{2}$ belongs to $D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c,{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(X,\mathbf{k})$, and $n\in\mathbf{Z}_{\geq 1}$ such that $H_{n}$ acts trivially on $X$, and replace diagram (A.4) by the similar diagram

$\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}\times X\leftarrow{G_{\mathcal{K}}}/H_{n}\times X\to({G_{\mathcal{K}}}/H_{n})\times^{({G_{\mathcal{O}}}/H_{n})}X\to\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},$

and proceed as before. In the body of the paper, as in [MV2], to lighten the notation we neglect these technical subtleties.

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
